title: SOV Word Order and the Copula (होना)
subtitle: Master the basic sentence structure and forms of 'to be' in present tense
keyPoint: Hindi follows a strict Subject-Object-Verb (SOV) sentence order where the inflected present copula always appears at the very end.

examples.en: मैं एक विद्यार्थी हूँ।
वह लड़का बहुत खुश है।
तुम बहुत अच्छे दोस्त हो।
हम सब भारतीय हैं।
यह मेरा कमरा है।

mistakes.note: Hindi verbs belong strictly at the end of the sentence (SOV), not directly after the subject like in English.
The polite second-person pronoun आप always requires the plural nasalized copula हैं, never singular है.
The auxiliary हो is reserved exclusively for तुम; हम requires हैं.

quiz.question: Choose the correct copula: 'मैं अध्यापक _____।'
quiz.explanation: The pronoun मैं ('I') always pairs uniquely with हूँ.

quiz.question: Choose the correct copula: 'आप बहुत दयालु _____।'
quiz.explanation: The formal pronoun आप always takes the plural/honorific copula हैं.

quiz.question: Choose the correct copula: 'तुम कहाँ _____?'
quiz.explanation: The informal pronoun तुम strictly pairs with the copula form हो.

quiz.question: Choose the correct copula: 'यह नया घर _____।'
quiz.explanation: Singular third-person entities (यह/वह) take the singular copula है.

tip: Listen carefully for the nasal dot (bindu) in हैं—it distinguishes the plural/formal 'are' from the singular unnasalized है 'is'.

title: Noun Gender and Direct-Case Marked Inflection
subtitle: Determine masculine and feminine nouns and adjust endings for plurals
keyPoint: Marked masculine nouns ending in -ा change to -े in the plural, while feminine nouns ending in -ी typically shorten to -िया for plurals.

examples.en: यह बड़ा कमरा साफ़ है।
ये दोनों कमरे बड़े हैं।
वह लड़की खेल रही है।
यहाँ बहुत सारी लड़कियाँ हैं।
मेज पर दो नई किताबें हैं।

mistakes.note: Marked masculine nouns ending in -ा must change to -े in the direct plural.
Feminine nouns ending in -ी must form their direct plural by shortening to -िया (लड़कियाँ).
Unmarked masculine nouns ending in consonants (like घर, सेब) do not change form in the direct plural.

quiz.question: What is the plural of the masculine noun 'कमरा' (room)?
quiz.explanation: Marked masculine nouns ending in -ा change to -े in the direct plural.

quiz.question: What is the plural of the feminine noun 'गाड़ी' (car)?
quiz.explanation: Feminine nouns ending in -ी change their final vowel to short -ि and add -याँ in the direct plural.

quiz.question: What is the plural of the unmarked masculine noun 'सेब' (apple) in the direct case?
quiz.explanation: Masculine nouns not ending in -ा remain completely unchanged in the direct plural.

quiz.question: What is the plural of the feminine noun 'रात' (night)?
quiz.explanation: Feminine consonant-ending nouns take -ें in the direct plural.

tip: Adjectives follow their nouns! A marked adjective like बड़ा changes to बड़े before plural masculine nouns and बड़ी before all feminine nouns.

title: Core Postpositions and the Oblique Case
subtitle: Inflect nouns and modifiers before Hindi case markers like में, पर, and से
keyPoint: Any noun or modifier followed directly by a postposition (में, पर, से, को, का) switches into the oblique case.

examples.en: उस लड़के को पानी दो।
बच्चे कमरे में खेल रहे हैं।
सभी लड़कों ने मेहनत की।
किताब उस मेज़ पर रखी है।
इन लड़कियों से पूछिए।

mistakes.note: The marked masculine noun कमरा must change to its oblique form कमरे before the postposition में.
Before the postposition को, marked masculine nouns ending in -ा obligatorily change to -े.
All plural nouns take the oblique ending -ों when followed by any postposition.

quiz.question: Fill in the blank with the correct oblique form: 'उस _____ में कोई नहीं है।' (कमरा - room)
quiz.explanation: The marked masculine noun कमरा changes to oblique कमरे before the postposition में.

quiz.question: Fill in the blank with the plural oblique form: 'इन _____ को खाना दो।' (बच्चा - child)
quiz.explanation: Plural nouns in the oblique case universally take the suffix -ों (बच्चों).

quiz.question: Fill in the blank: 'वह _____ पर बैठी है।' (कुर्सी - chair)
quiz.explanation: Feminine singular nouns ending in -ी do not change form in the singular oblique.

quiz.question: Fill in the blank: 'सब _____ से बात करो।' (दोस्त - friend [plural])
quiz.explanation: Even unmarked masculine nouns take -ों in the plural oblique case before postpositions like से.

tip: English uses prepositions placed BEFORE nouns (in the room), but Hindi uses postpositions placed AFTER (कमरे में). Watch out for that automatic oblique shift on the preceding word!

title: Present Habitual Aspect (ता/ती/ते है)
subtitle: Express daily routines and general truths with the imperfective participle
keyPoint: Add -ता, -ती, or -ते to the verb stem based on gender and number, followed by the present copula (हूँ, है, हो, हैं).

useCases.label: Daily Routine
useCases.example: मैं रोज़ सुबह छह बजे उठता हूँ।

useCases.label: General Preferences
useCases.example: हम शाम को चाय पीते हैं।

examples.en: अमित रोज़ स्कूल जाता है।
नेहा हर दिन हिंदी पढ़ती है।
हम दिल्ली में रहते हैं।
तुम कहाँ काम करते हो?
लड़कियाँ यहाँ खेलती हैं।

mistakes.note: Do not drop the present auxiliary हूँ; habitual present requires stem + participle + copula.
The participle must agree with the feminine subject सीता, using -ती instead of -ता.
Plural masculine third-person subjects take -ते on the verb participle (रहते), not -ता.

quiz.question: Complete the sentence for a female speaker: 'मैं रोज़ सुबह दौड़ने _____।'
quiz.explanation: A female speaker uses the feminine participle ending -ती paired with हूँ.

quiz.question: Complete the sentence: 'सूरज सुबह _____।'
quiz.explanation: सूरज (sun) is masculine singular, so it triggers उगता है.

quiz.question: Complete the sentence: 'आप कहाँ _____?' (addressing a male elder)
quiz.explanation: The formal pronoun आप takes the masculine plural honorific participle ending -ते and auxiliary हैं.

quiz.question: Complete the sentence: 'तुम क्या _____?' (to a male peer)
quiz.explanation: The pronoun तुम pairs with masculine plural/informal participle -ते and the copula हो.

tip: To make any habitual sentence negative, insert नहीं right before the participle verb phrase (e.g. मैं चाय नहीं पीता), where the final auxiliary है/हूँ is frequently dropped!

title: Continuous Aspect with रहा/रही/रहे
subtitle: Describe actions unfolding in real time using root + रहा/रही/रहे + auxiliary
keyPoint: Form the continuous aspect by joining the bare verb root with रहा/रही/रहे, inflected to match the subject's gender and number, followed by the copula.

useCases.label: Temporary Contemporary States
useCases.example: मैं इन दिनों एक किताब लिख रहा हूँ।

examples.en: मोहन अभी खाना खा रहा है।
पूजा गाना सुन रही है।
हम बाज़ार जा रहे हैं।
लड़कियाँ हँस रही हैं।
आप क्या पढ़ रहे हैं?

mistakes.note: Attach रहा directly to the bare verb root (पी), not to the habitual participle (पीता).
A feminine plural subject requires रही with the nasalized auxiliary हैं (never रहे हैं).
In affirmative present continuous sentences, do not omit the present auxiliary हूँ/है/हैं.

quiz.question: Complete the sentence: 'रोहन गेंद फेंक _____।'
quiz.explanation: रोहन is masculine singular, requiring रहा है.

quiz.question: Complete the sentence for a female speaker: 'मैं अपनी सहेली को पत्र लिख _____।'
quiz.explanation: A female speaker (मैं) uses रही with the first-person copula हूँ.

quiz.question: Complete the sentence: 'माताजी खाना बना _____।'
quiz.explanation: माताजी is a respected female singular entity, triggering honorific feminine agreement रही हैं.

quiz.question: Complete the sentence: 'बच्चे मैदान में दौड़ _____।'
quiz.explanation: बच्चे is masculine plural, requiring रहे हैं.

tip: Unlike habitual aspect where feminine plural takes an overt nasal marker on the participle (-तीं), the continuous marker stays uniform as रही, leaving the nasalization solely on the auxiliary: रही हैं.

title: Imperative Forms and Politeness Tiers
subtitle: Master the three politeness levels: तू, तुम, and आप
keyPoint: Hindi commands change endings based on social distance, moving from the bare root with intimate तू to -ओ with informal तुम and -इए with polite आप.

cells: Children, close friends, or deity; offensive if used carelessly
Elders, professionals, strangers, and formal respect

examples.en: आप चाय पीजिए।
तुम बाज़ार जाओ और फल लाओ।
यहाँ हस्ताक्षर कीजिए।
दरवाज़ा बंद करो।
तू चुप रह।

mistakes.note: Do not mix the respectful pronoun आप with the informal -ओ verb ending; always match आप with -इए or -ईजिए.
When using the formal request word 'कृपया' (please), always use the polite imperative tier (-इए).
The irregular polite command for पीना is पीजिए, but the तुम form is straightforwardly पियो.

quiz.question: Polite request to an elder: 'Please come inside.' -> कृपया अंदर ___।
quiz.explanation: For respectful address (matching आप/कृपया), append -इए to the verb stem.

quiz.question: Casual instruction to a classmate: 'Read this book.' -> यह किताब ___।
quiz.explanation: Talking familiarly to peers uses the तुम tier, ending in -ओ (पढ़ + ओ = पढ़ो).

quiz.question: Formal command: 'Please take this cup.' -> यह कप ___।
quiz.explanation: The verb लेना has the irregular polite command रूप लीजिए rather than लेइए.

quiz.question: Intimate instruction to a small child: 'Eat food quickly.' -> जल्दी खाना ___।
quiz.explanation: The intimate तू imperative simply takes the bare verb stem (खा).

tip: Four high-frequency verbs have irregular polite (आप) forms: करना becomes कीजिए, लेना becomes लीजिए, देना becomes दीजिए, and पीना becomes पीजिए.

title: Ergative Case Alignment with ने
subtitle: Transitive verbs in perfective tenses transfer agreement to the object
keyPoint: In perfective tenses of transitive verbs, the subject takes the postposition ने and the verb agrees in gender and number with the unmarked direct object.

useCases.label: Completed Transitive Action
useCases.example: राधा ने एक सुंदर गीत गाया।

examples.en: अमित ने एक नया घर खरीदा।
माँ ने स्वादिष्ट चाय बनाई।
छात्रों ने कठिन सवाल पूछे।
सीता ने एक पत्र लिखा।
हमने ताज़ा रोटियाँ खाईं।

mistakes.note: Because ने is on the subject, the verb must agree with the object सेब (masculine singular), not the subject लड़की.
The pronoun वह changes to oblique form उस before ने (producing उसने).
जाना (to go) is intransitive and never takes ने, even in the past perfective tense.

quiz.question: Complete the sentence: 'Neha wrote a letter.' -> नेहा ने पत्र ___।
quiz.explanation: The direct object पत्र is masculine singular, so the verb agrees with it: लिखा.

quiz.question: Identify the correct ergative pronoun: '___ saw the film.'
quiz.explanation: In transitive perfective clauses, the subject 'we' takes the ergative postposition: हमने.

quiz.question: Which verb NEVER takes ने in the past tense?
quiz.explanation: लाना (to bring) is grammatically treated as intransitive in Hindi and never takes ने.

quiz.question: Complete the sentence: 'The boy read two books.' -> लड़के ने दो किताबें ___।
quiz.explanation: किताबें is feminine plural, so the verb agrees with feminine plural nasalized inflection पढ़ीं.

tip: Remember: लाना (to bring), भूलना (to forget), and बोलना (to speak) generally do not take ने, behaving like intransitive verbs.

title: Differential Object Marking with को
subtitle: Specific and animate direct objects take को and neutralize verb agreement
keyPoint: Direct objects that are human, animate, or specifically identified require the postposition को, which triggers the default masculine singular ending on the verb in perfective clauses.

cells: No को needed; verb agrees with object
को blocks agreement; verb reverts to default -आ
Even feminine noun takes masculine singular default verb
Personal pronouns as direct objects always take को

examples.en: माँ ने बच्चे को जगाया।
मैंने उस लड़की को देखा।
अध्यापक ने छात्रों को बुलाया।
सुरेश ने बिल्ली को बचाया।
उसने इस फ़िल्म को पसंद किया।

mistakes.note: When the direct object is marked with को, it cannot trigger agreement; the verb must freeze in the default masculine singular -आ form.
Indefinite, generic, inanimate objects should not take को.
Before the postposition को, nouns and demonstrative adjectives must enter the oblique case (उस लड़के).

quiz.question: Identify the correct form: 'The mother called the daughter.' -> माँ ने बेटी को ___।
quiz.explanation: Because बेटी is marked with को, agreement is blocked, forcing the default masculine singular ending बुलाया.

quiz.question: Which object requires को? 'I saw ___.'
quiz.explanation: अध्यापक is a human being, and animate/human direct objects obligatorily take differential object marking with को.

quiz.question: Choose the correct sentence: 'Call Ramesh.'
quiz.explanation: Specific individual names functioning as direct objects take को: रमेश को बुलाओ।

quiz.question: What happens when both the subject has ने and the object has को?
options: Verb takes default masculine singular ending
quiz.explanation: When both core arguments are postpositionally marked, verb agreement defaults to masculine singular (-आ).

tip: Double-blocked agreement rule: When the subject takes ने and the object takes को, the verb ALWAYS defaults to masculine singular (-आ), regardless of either noun's actual gender.

title: Dative Subject (Experiencer) Constructions
subtitle: Express feelings, physical states, and needs with Subject + को
keyPoint: In involuntary experiences, sensations, or psychological states, the experiencer is marked with को while the grammatical agreement is controlled by the sensation or thing experienced.

useCases.label: Knowledge & Mental States
useCases.example: क्या आपको यह बात मालूम है?

examples.en: मुझे ठंड लग रही है।
पिताजी को सिरदर्द है।
हमें आपकी मदद चाहिए।
क्या तुमको हिंदी आती है?
अनीता को गुस्सा आया।

mistakes.note: Hunger is an involuntary experience; the experiencer takes मुझे (मैं + को), not the nominative मैं.
Expressions of need with dative experiencers use the defective modal verb रूप चाहिए, not regular conjugations of चाहना.
While plural agreement can sometimes be heard colloquially, standard चाहिए remains invariant with dative subjects.

quiz.question: Express: 'I know this.' -> ___ यह मालूम है।
quiz.explanation: मालूम होना (to be known) requires an experiencer marked with को (मैं + को = मुझे).

quiz.question: Express: 'Do you feel cold?' -> क्या आपको ठंड ___?
quiz.explanation: ठंड is feminine singular, so the verb agrees with it: लग रही है.

quiz.question: Complete the need sentence: 'The student needs a pen.' -> छात्र को कलम ___।
quiz.explanation: Expressing that someone requires an object uses Experiencer + को + Object + चाहिए.

quiz.question: Which sentence means 'I like Hindi'?
quiz.explanation: पसंद होना takes a dative experiencer: मुझे हिंदी पसंद है।

tip: Combine personal pronouns with को into short contracted forms: मुझे (not मुझको), तुझे (not तुझको), उसे (not उसको), and हमें (not हमकों).

title: Possession Systems: का vs के पास
subtitle: Distinguish portable property from kinship and body parts
keyPoint: Use के पास for alienable, tangible, or movable possession (like money or phones), but inflected forms of का (का/की/के) for inalienable kinship ties, body parts, and intrinsic qualities.

cells: के पास is invariant; verb agrees with possessed item
Genitive postposition agrees with the relative in gender/number
हाथी की लंबी सूँड़ होती है
Belongs inherently to the subject; inflects like an adjective
Concrete availability uses के पास; quality takes का

examples.en: मेरे पास एक मोबाइल फ़ोन है।
रोहन के दो भाई हैं।
क्या आपके पास चाबी है?
गाय के चार पैर होते हैं।
हमारे पास आज गाड़ी नहीं है।

mistakes.note: Family members cannot be held as portable items; use the possessive genitive मेरे, not मेरे पास.
Body parts are inalienable and naturally attached, requiring का/के/की rather than के पास.
The postposition complex is fixed as के पास, so feminine possessors still take masculine oblique के (सीमा के पास).

quiz.question: Express: 'I have a car.' -> ___ एक कार है।
quiz.explanation: A car is a movable, alienable object; use the locative-possessive construct मेरे पास.

quiz.question: Express: 'Ravi has two sisters.' -> रवि ___ दो बहनें हैं।
quiz.explanation: Sisters (बहनें) are feminine plural relatives, requiring the feminine genitive marker की.

quiz.question: Express: 'Do you have pen with you right now?' -> क्या आपके ___ कलम है?
quiz.explanation: Tangible possession uses the compound postposition के पास.

quiz.question: Choose the natural sentence for 'Cats have sharp teeth.'
options: बिल्ली के पास तेज़ दाँत होते हैं।
बिल्ली के तेज़ दाँत होते हैं।
बिल्ली को तेज़ दाँत होते हैं।
बिल्ली में तेज़ दाँत होते हैं।
quiz.explanation: Teeth are inalienable body parts, so use the genitive marker के rather than के पास.

tip: Test it simply: If you can accidentally leave it at home in a drawer, use 'के पास'. If it is part of your anatomy or family tree, use 'का / के / की'.

title: Modals of Obligation (पड़ना vs होना)
subtitle: Expressing internal necessity versus external compulsion in dative constructions
keyPoint: Mark the logical subject with the dative postposition को and use an infinitive with होना for planned duty, or with पड़ना for involuntary external compulsion.

cells: I had to stay late (forced/no choice).
He will have to pay a fine.
Verb agrees with object (or default masc. sing.)

useCases.label: Scheduled Obligation
useCases.example: रोहन को कल दिल्ली जाना है।

useCases.label: Involuntary Duty
useCases.example: बारिश के कारण हमें पैदल चलना पड़ा।

examples.en: मुझे रोज़ सुबह छह बजे उठना पड़ता है।
अमित को आज शाम को डॉक्टर के पास जाना है।
हमें मजबूरी में यह पुराना घर बेचना पड़ा।
तुम्हें इस कठिन परीक्षा के लिए बहुत मेहनत करनी होगी।
छात्रों को गृहकार्य समय पर जमा करना पड़ेगा।

mistakes.note: The logical subject must take the dative marker को (मैं + को becomes मुझे).
Because चाय is feminine singular, the infinitive and auxiliary agree with it (पीनी है).

mistakes.right: मुझे रोज़ काम करना पड़ता है।
mistakes.note: To express routine obligation or compulsion, use पड़ना, not चाहना.

quiz.question: Because the car broke down, 'We had to walk.'
quiz.explanation: External involuntary obligation in the past requires the subject with को (हमें) and infinitive + पड़ा.

quiz.question: Choose the correct sentence for 'I have to write a letter (routine/duty)':
quiz.explanation: The subject takes मुझे, and masculine singular ख़त requires the masculine infinitive and verb agreement लिखना है.

quiz.question: Fill in the blank for unavoidable future consequence: 'तुम्हें यह दवाई कड़वी होने पर भी लेनी ___।' (fem. sing.)
quiz.explanation: दवाई is feminine singular, so the future compulsion verb पड़ना inflects as पड़ेगी.

quiz.question: Which sentence expresses that Priya is obliged by schedule (not coercion) to leave at 5?
options: प्रिया को पाँच बजे जाना पड़ा।
प्रिया को पाँच बजे जाना पड़ेगा।
प्रिया को पाँच बजे जाना है।
quiz.explanation: The infinitive + होना construction indicates scheduled or accepted personal plans without forced external pressure.

tip: Think of पड़ना as 'falling upon someone' (external burden) and होना as an established state or agenda.

title: Synthetic Future Tense Conjugation
subtitle: Forming future actions using direct stem inflections with gender and number suffixes
keyPoint: Add personal subjunctive suffixes to the verb stem followed by गा, गी, or गे depending on the subject's gender and grammatical number.

useCases.label: Definite Future Intent
useCases.example: हम अगले हफ़्ते नया मकान ख़रीदेंगे।

useCases.label: Promises and Commitments
useCases.example: मैं कल समय पर तुम्हारा काम कर दूँगा।

examples.en: सुनीता कल शाम को बाज़ार जाएगी।
क्या आप हमारे साथ दोपहर का खाना खाएंगे?
लड़के मैदान में क्रिकेट खेलेंगे।
मैं यह नई किताब दो दिनों में पढ़ लूँगी।
पिताजी दफ़्तर से कब लौटेंगे?

mistakes.note: हम represents plural first-person and requires the plural ending -एंगे / -एंगी, not singular -एगा.
Feminine plural subjects require nasalized -एंगी ending.
The pronoun मैं combines with verb stems ending in -ऊँगा / -ऊँगी, never -एगा.

quiz.question: Identify the correct feminine form: 'सीमा कल एक पत्र ___।' (लिखना)
quiz.explanation: Third-person singular feminine requires the suffix -एगी (लिखेगी).

quiz.question: Complete the sentence: 'हम कल सिनेमा ___।' (जाना, masculine plural)
quiz.explanation: हम (masculine plural) takes the synthetic suffix -एंगे giving जाएंगे.

quiz.question: Which form matches a woman saying 'I will speak': 'मैं हिन्दी में ___।'?
quiz.explanation: A female first-person speaker uses stem + -ऊँगी, making बोलूँगी.

quiz.question: Which verb form correctly completes the formal question: 'आप चाय ___?' (पीना)
quiz.explanation: आप takes the respectful plural ending -एंगे (पिएंगे) or -एंगी (पिएंगी). Option 3 is misspelled relative to standard masculine formal plural.

tip: The irregular forms for stems ending in vowels often contract smoothly: देना becomes दूँगा/देंगे and लेना becomes लूँगा/लेंगे.

title: Compound Verbs with Polar Explanators (लेना, देना, जाना, डालना)
subtitle: Nuancing root verbs with auxiliary operators for completion, direction, and intensity
keyPoint: A compound verb joins a bare main verb stem with an inflected auxiliary operator that adds aspectual nuances such as self-benefit (लेना), other-benefit (देना), or totality (जाना).

cells: to fall down / to eat up

useCases.label: Self-Directed Benefit
useCases.example: उसने सारा खाना चुपचाप खा लिया।

useCases.label: Other-Directed Action
useCases.example: शिक्षक ने छात्रों को नया पाठ समझा दिया।

useCases.label: Drastic Complete Action
useCases.example: गुस्से में उसने वह पुराना पत्र फाड़ डाला।

examples.en: मैंने सारा सच अपनी माँ को बता दिया।
बच्चों ने अपने सारे खिलौने समेट लिए।
गिलास मेज़ से नीचे गिर गया।
डाकुओं ने सिपाही को गोली से मार डाला।
दुकानदार ने अपना सारा सामान बेच दिया।

mistakes.note: When the action is performed for another person's benefit, use देना (दी), not लेना.
Intransitive change-of-state verbs combine with जाना (गिर गया), not transitive लेना.

mistakes.right: मैं खाना खा गया। (or मैंने खाना खा लिया।)
mistakes.note: When using जाना as an operator, the whole compound functions intransitively for ergative marking; do not use ने with खा जाना.

quiz.question: Which compound verb correctly expresses 'I explained it (for someone else)': 'मैंने मित्र को बात ___।'?
quiz.explanation: देना conveys actions directed outward toward or for the benefit of another person.

quiz.question: Choose the form emphasizing that the cat ate up all the fish completely and irreversibly:
options: बिल्ली ने सारी मछली खा दी।
quiz.explanation: खा जाना indicates total consumption and completion without retaining ergative ने.

quiz.question: What nuance does डालना add in 'उसने शीशा तोड़ डाला'?
quiz.explanation: The operator डालना imparts a sense of violence, sudden force, rashness, or utter disregard.

quiz.question: Select the correct combination for 'She kept/took the money for herself': 'उसने पैसे ___।'?
quiz.explanation: The operator लेना (plural masculine लिए agreeing with पैसे) indicates self-directed retention.

tip: Only the second verb (the operator) conjugates for tense, aspect, and gender; the main root remains in its bare stem form.

title: Conjunctive Participle Construction with कर (Kar)
subtitle: Chaining chronologically ordered actions with bare verb stems plus कर or के
keyPoint: Attach कर or के directly to a verb stem to combine sequential clauses that share the exact same grammatical subject.

useCases.label: Sequential Actions
useCases.example: वह नहाकर पूजा करने मंदिर गया।

useCases.label: Cause and Effect Manner
useCases.example: समाचार सुनकर वह बहुत खुश हुआ।

examples.en: मैं दफ़्तर पहुँचकर तुम्हें फ़ोन करूँगा।
छात्र गृहकार्य समाप्त करके सोने चले गए।
उसने दौड़कर बस पकड़ी।
हम बाज़ार से सब्ज़ियाँ लाकर खाना बनाएंगे।
पिताजी चाय पीकर अख़बार पढ़ने लगे।

mistakes.note: With the verb करना, repeat Avoidance requires करके instead of करकर.

mistakes.wrong: मैंने खाया और मैं सो गया। (redundant in natural speech)
mistakes.note: Native speakers condense redundant sequential coordinate clauses into a single conjunctive participle sentence with कर.

mistakes.wrong: मेरे जाने कर वह रोने लगी।
mistakes.right: मेरे जाने पर वह रोने लगी।
mistakes.note: Both actions in a कर construction must share the exact same subject; if subjects differ, use a postpositional participle like पर instead.

quiz.question: Join these two actions: 'वह घर आया' and 'उसने खाना खाया':
options: उसने घर आते ही खाना खाया था।
quiz.explanation: The main clause verb खाया requires the ergative उसने, while the first clause collapses into आकर.

quiz.question: How should the verb करना be formed as a conjunctive participle?
quiz.explanation: The verb stem कर- irregular pairs with -के to yield करके to prevent sound repetition.

quiz.question: Complete the sentence: 'राधा रोते हुए बच्चे को ___ हँसाने लगी।' (देखना)
quiz.explanation: The sequential action 'on seeing' is expressed by the stem देख plus कर: देखकर.

quiz.question: Which sentence demonstrates the use of a conjunctive participle indicating manner?
quiz.explanation: भागकर ('by running') acts as a conjunctive participle detailing how the primary action was performed.

tip: If the main clause takes an ergative marker ने, apply it to the shared subject at the very start of the sentence (e.g., उसने चाय पीकर काम शुरू किया).

title: Subjunctive Mood for Contingency and Wishes
subtitle: Conveying possibility, polite requests, desires, and uncertain conditions
keyPoint: Drop the final future particles (गा/गी/गे) to yield the tenseless subjunctive endings that express doubts, indirect requests, and contingent possibilities.

useCases.label: Uncertainty with 'शायद' (Perhaps)
useCases.example: शायद आज रात को बारिश हो।

useCases.label: Desire / Purpose Clauses with 'ताकि'
useCases.example: मेहनत करो ताकि तुम सफल हो सको।

examples.en: अगर वह यहाँ आए तो मुझे तुरंत बताना।
क्या मैं अंदर आऊँ?
भगवान करे आपकी हर मनोकामना पूरी हो।
शायद वे कल हमसे मिलने आएँ।
मैं चाहता हूँ कि तुम हमेशा सच बोलो।

mistakes.note: Words of doubt such as शायद canonically trigger the subjunctive (आए) rather than the indicative future (आएगा).
When asking for polite permission ('May I come in?'), Hindi requires the subjunctive आऊँ, not the future declaration आऊँगा.

mistakes.wrong: अगर आप बोलेगा तो मैं सुनूँगा।
mistakes.right: अगर आप बोलें तो मैं सुनूँगा।
mistakes.note: Formal आप takes the nasalized subjunctive suffix -एँ (बोलें) in conditional prototypes.

quiz.question: How do you ask 'Shall we leave now?' politely in Hindi?
quiz.explanation: First-person plural subjunctive चलें expresses a polite collective suggestion or inquiry.

quiz.question: Select the correct verb form expressing possibility: 'संभव है कि वह आज न ___।' (आना)
quiz.explanation: Expressions of contingency like 'संभव है कि' govern the subjunctive verb mood (आए).

quiz.question: Complete the polite request to enter: 'क्या मैं खिड़की खोल ___?' (देना)
quiz.explanation: The first-person singular subjunctive of देना is दूँ ('May I open/give?').

quiz.question: Choose the correct verb for a wish: 'मेरी इच्छा है कि आप हमारे घर ___।' (पधारना)
quiz.explanation: Wishes introduced by इच्छा है कि require the subjunctive form agreeing with आप (पधारें).

tip: To easily form the subjunctive, start with the synthetic future tense and simply strip off the trailing गा, गी, or गे.

title: First and Second Causative Verb Formations
subtitle: Transforming base verbs into direct and indirect causative actions
keyPoint: Hindi creates first causatives by adding -आना to cause an action directly, and second causatives with -वाना to have an action done via an intermediary.

cells: to have done / cause to do

useCases.label: Direct Causation
useCases.example: माँ बच्चे को खाना खिलाती है।

useCases.label: Indirect Mediation
useCases.example: अध्यापक छात्रों से निबंध लिखवाते हैं।

useCases.label: Vowel Shortening Shift
useCases.example: वह बढ़ई से मेज़ बनवाता है।

examples.en: माँ बच्चे को सुलाती है।
पिताजी दर्ज़ी से कपड़े सिलवाते हैं।
मालिक नौकर से कमरा साफ़ करवाता है।
मैं तुम्हें यह नया गाना सुनाता हूँ।
उसने मैकेनिक से गाड़ी ठीक करवाई।

mistakes.note: The root vowel in सोना (to sleep) shifts to short 'उ' and inserts 'ल' to form सुलाना, rather than regular suffixation.

mistakes.wrong: मैं दोस्त से चाय बनाता हूँ।
mistakes.right: मैं दोस्त से चाय बनवाता हूँ।
mistakes.note: Use the second causative (बनवाना) when using a secondary agent marked with से.
Having an intermediary perform an action requires the causative stem धुलवाना, agreeing with plural masculine कपड़े.

quiz.question: Choose the correct first causative form: 'The teacher teaches (makes learn) the students.' -> अध्यापक बच्चों को ___ हैं।
quiz.explanation: The base verb सीखना (to learn) shortens its root vowel to 'इ' and adds -आना to form सिखाना for direct causation.

quiz.question: Choose the correct second causative: 'I get the house painted by a painter.' -> मैं पेंटर से घर ___ हूँ।
quiz.explanation: Indirect causation involving an agent with से requires the second causative suffix -वाना, yielding रँगवाना.

quiz.question: Identify the base intransitive form of the causative verb 'दिखाना' (to show):
quiz.explanation: दिखना (to be seen/visible) is the base intransitive verb, from which the transitive देखना and causatives are derived.

quiz.question: Complete the sentence: 'She had her luggage lifted by the porter.' -> उसने कुली से सामान ___।
quiz.explanation: With an intermediary agent marked with से (कुली से), the second causative perfective masculine singular उठवाया is required.

tip: Long vowels in monosyllabic roots always shorten when causativized: आ becomes अ, ई becomes इ, and ऊ becomes उ.

title: Passive Voice and Expressions of Inability with जाना
subtitle: Forming objective passives and instrumental expressions of incapacity
keyPoint: The passive voice is formed by combining the perfective participle of the main verb with inflected forms of जाना.

cells: Agent + के द्वारा / से + Verb + जाना
The thief was caught by police

useCases.label: Physical Incapacity
useCases.example: दादी जी से सीढ़ियाँ नहीं चढ़ी जातीं।

examples.en: यहाँ रोज़ ताज़ा खाना पकाया जाता है।
यह पुल पिछले साल बनाया गया।
मुझसे इतना तीखा खाना नहीं खाया जाता।
मरीज़ से अब उठा नहीं जाता।
सारे समाचार पत्र पढ़े जा चुके हैं।

mistakes.note: Hindi passive voice requires the auxiliary verb जाना, never होना.
The agent in passives of physical incapacity must take the postposition से, not को.
Both the main perfective participle and जाना must agree in gender and number with the promoted subject (किताबें = fem. pl.).

quiz.question: Complete the passive sentence: 'Hindi is understood throughout India.' -> पूरे भारत में हिंदी ___।
quiz.explanation: हिंदी is feminine singular, so the perfective participle and auxiliary must be feminine singular: समझी जाती है.

quiz.question: How do you express 'I cannot walk (due to physical inability)'?
quiz.explanation: Agent + से + intransitive perfective participle + नहीं + जाना expresses involuntary incapacity.

quiz.question: Complete the sentence: 'The thief was arrested by the police.' -> पुलिस के द्वारा चोर ___।
quiz.explanation: चोर is masculine singular here as the grammatical subject, requiring पकड़ा गया.

quiz.question: Fill in the blank: 'Old houses are being demolished.' -> पुराने मकान गिराए ___।
quiz.explanation: मकान is masculine plural and the context indicates continuous passive, demanding गिराए जा रहे हैं.

tip: In passives expressing incapacity (असमर्थता), even intransitive verbs like चलना, उठना, or सोना can be used with a default masculine singular ending.

title: Relative-Correlative Syntactic Structures (जो... वो, जब... तब)
subtitle: Pairing relative and correlative markers to construct compound sentences
keyPoint: Hindi relative clauses introduce a condition or identity with a 'ज-' word and resolve it in the main clause with a corresponding 'त-' or 'व-' correlative word.

cells: As / As much... so / that much

useCases.label: Individual Identification
useCases.example: जो लड़का वहाँ खड़ा है, वह मेरा भाई है।

useCases.label: Temporal Dependency
useCases.example: जब बारिश रुकी, तब हम बाहर गए।

useCases.label: Proportional Comparison
useCases.example: जितनी मेहनत करोगे, उतनी सफलता मिलेगी।

examples.en: जो मेहनत करता है, वह हमेशा सफल होता है।
जब मैं स्टेशन पहुँचा, तब गाड़ी आ चुकी थी।
जहाँ शांति होती है, वहाँ ईश्वर का वास होता है।
जैसा बोओगे, वैसा काटोगे।
जितना माँगो उतना लो।

mistakes.wrong: वह लड़का जो वहाँ खड़ा है, मेरा भाई है। (stylistically weak)
mistakes.right: जो लड़का वहाँ खड़ा है, वह मेरा भाई है।
mistakes.note: Natural Hindi syntax places the relative clause (with जो) first, followed by the correlative clause (with वह).

mistakes.wrong: जब बारिश होगी, मैं घर जाऊँगा।
mistakes.right: जब बारिश होगी, तब मैं घर जाऊँगा।
mistakes.note: Hindi requires the explicit correlative conjunction तब in the main clause; it cannot be dropped like 'then' in English.

mistakes.wrong: जितना तुम खाओगे, वैसा तुम बनोगे।
mistakes.right: जैसा तुम खाओगे, वैसा तुम बनोगे।
mistakes.note: Correlative pairs must match semantically: जैसा pairs with वैसा (manner/quality), and जितना pairs with उतना (quantity).

quiz.question: Complete the time clause: '___ तुम आओगे, तब हम खाना खाएँगे।'
quiz.explanation: The temporal correlative तब must be preceded by the temporal relative conjunction जब.

quiz.question: Complete the proportional clause: 'जितना गुड़ डालोगे, ___ मीठा होगा।'
quiz.explanation: The quantity relative जितना must pair with the correlative उतना.

quiz.question: Complete the clause: 'जहाँ फूल खिलते हैं, ___ भँवरे आते हैं।'
quiz.explanation: जहाँ denotes place and corresponds directly to वहाँ.

quiz.question: Fill in the blank: 'जो लड़की कल आई थी, ___ मेरी सहेली है।'
quiz.explanation: The relative pronoun जो referring to an entity is paired with the correlative pronoun वह/वो.

tip: Remember: ज-words introduce the dependent relative clause, and corresponding त- or व-words anchor the independent correlative clause.

title: Imperfective and Perfective Participles as Modifiers (हुआ/हुई/हुए)
subtitle: Employing expanded participial modifiers to describe ongoing or resultant noun states
keyPoint: Participles followed by forms of हुआ act as adjectives, agreeing in gender and number with the noun they modify to indicate ongoing or resultant states.

useCases.label: Active Continuous State
useCases.example: मैंने दौड़ती हुई गाड़ी को देखा।

useCases.label: Resultant Past State
useCases.example: मेज पर रखा हुआ पत्र पढ़ो।

useCases.label: Oblique Case Modification
useCases.example: उस गिरे हुए पेड़ को हटाओ।

examples.en: हँसती हुई लड़की कमरे में आई।
सड़क पर गिरे हुए पत्ते बहुत सुंदर लगते हैं।
अलमारी में रखी हुई किताबें पुरानी हैं।
मैंने तैरते हुए हंसों को देखा।
दीवार पर टँगी हुई तस्वीर गिर गई।

mistakes.right: मैंने एक टूटी हुई कुर्सी देखी।
mistakes.note: Participles modifying feminine nouns must show feminine agreement in both participle and auxiliary: टूटी हुई.

mistakes.wrong: सोता हुआ बच्चे को मत जगाओ।
mistakes.right: सोते हुए बच्चे को मत जगाओ।
mistakes.note: Because बच्चे is followed by the postposition को, the modifier must inflect to masculine oblique: सोते हुए.
In the direct singular nominative case, the imperfective adjectival modifier must be दौड़ता हुआ, not plural/oblique दौड़ते.

quiz.question: Complete the sentence with an adjectival participle: 'Bring the water boiling on the stove.' -> चूल्हे पर ___ पानी लाओ।
quiz.explanation: पानी is grammatically masculine singular direct here, requiring the masculine singular imperfective participle उबलता हुआ.

quiz.question: Select the correct form: 'Do not throw stones at the sleeping dog.' -> ___ कुत्ते पर पत्थर मत फेंको।
quiz.explanation: The noun कुत्ते is in the masculine oblique singular before पर, so the modifier must take the oblique form सोते हुए.

quiz.question: Fill in the blank: 'The flowers plucked from the garden have dried up.' -> बाग़ से ___ फूल सूख गए।
quiz.explanation: फूल is masculine plural in this subject position, requiring the masculine plural resultant form तोड़े हुए.

quiz.question: Fill in the blank: 'She was reading a written letter.' -> वह एक ___ चिट्ठी पढ़ रही थी।
quiz.explanation: चिट्ठी is feminine singular, so the resultant modifier must be feminine singular: लिखी हुई.

tip: Use the imperfective participle (ता हुआ) for an action currently in progress, and the perfective participle (आ हुआ) for a state that resulted from a completed event.

title: Presumptive (होगा) and Counterfactual Past Tenses
subtitle: Deducing epistemic probability with होगा and expressing unfulfilled past conditions
keyPoint: The presumptive mood uses participles with होगा to express probabilities, while the counterfactual uses bare imperfective participles in both clauses to express unfulfilled conditions.

cells: He must be studying / probably studies
यदि तुम आते, तो मैं चलता
Had you come, I would have gone

useCases.label: Epistemic Inference
useCases.example: वह अब तक घर पहुँच गया होगा।

useCases.label: Habitual Assumption
useCases.example: रोहन दफ़्तर में काम करता होगा।

useCases.label: Unfulfilled Past Condition
useCases.example: अगर बारिश होती, तो फ़सल अच्छी होती।

examples.en: पिताजी इस समय अख़बार पढ़ रहे होंगे।
डाकिया अब तक चिट्ठी दे चुका होगा।
यदि तुम मुझे बताते, तो मैं तुम्हारी मदद करता।
examples.highlight: बताते, तो मैं तुम्हारी मदद करता

examples.en: अगर हम समय पर निकलते, तो ट्रेन न छूटती।
उसने यह फ़िल्म ज़रूर देखी होगी।

mistakes.wrong: अगर तुम आते, तो मैं आऊँगा।
mistakes.right: अगर तुम आते, तो मैं आता।
mistakes.note: In a counterfactual past conditional, both the protasis and apodosis must use bare imperfective participles, never the future tense.
Do not stack present auxiliary है with the presumptive auxiliary होगा; attach होगा directly to the perfective participle.

mistakes.wrong: यदि बारिश होती, तो फ़सल अच्छी होगी।
mistakes.right: यदि बारिश होती, तो फ़सल अच्छी होती।
mistakes.note: Counterfactual outcomes require the past imperfective participle होती to denote unfulfilled past possibility.

quiz.question: Express epistemic presumption: 'She must have reached Delhi by now.' -> वह अब तक दिल्ली ___।
quiz.explanation: The feminine perfective participle पहुँच गई plus feminine singular presumptive auxiliary होगी conveys 'must have arrived'.

quiz.question: Complete the counterfactual sentence: 'If you had studied, you would have passed.' -> अगर तुम पढ़ते, तो परीक्षा में सफल ___।
quiz.explanation: Hindi past counterfactuals take the bare imperfective participle (होते) in the result clause.

quiz.question: Express habitual presumption: 'What does he do at this hour?' -> वह इस समय क्या ___?
quiz.explanation: Habitual presumptive is formed with the imperfective participle करता plus presumptive auxiliary होगा.

quiz.question: Complete the negative counterfactual: 'Had we run fast, the bus would not have been missed.' -> यदि हम तेज़ दौड़ते, तो बस ___।
quiz.explanation: The negative unfulfilled counterfactual uses the negative particle न (or नहीं) alongside the bare participle छूटती.

tip: For unfulfilled past regrets or 'what ifs', drop all forms of 'था' and 'है' — use only the bare -ता/-ती/-ते participle in both parts of the sentence.
